items.stem: Which of the following best describes "sovereignty"?
options: States working together through agreements and institutions to manage shared risks
The authority of a state to govern itself without outside interference
A narrow passage on a major trade route, such as the Strait of Malacca, Suez Canal or Strait of Hormuz
A state whose government has lost control of its territory and cannot provide basic services or security
items.answer: The authority of a state to govern itself without outside interference
items.markingKey: B. "sovereignty" is the authority of a state to govern itself without outside interference.

items.stem: Mateo writes: "Globalisation always reduces conflict." Explain why this is inaccurate.

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain how conflict disrupts global interactions.
items.answer: It destroys infrastructure, closes trade routes and airspace, deters investment and tourism, displaces people, and triggers sanctions, e.g. the war in Ukraine disrupted grain, energy and fertiliser exports. items.stem: Brazil imposes a 25% tariff on imported solar panels. The world price is US$120 per panel. Imports were 570 thousand panels a year and fall by 15% after the tariff. Calculate the import price including the tariff and the annual tariff revenue (US$ million).

items.stem: "Globalisation has reduced national sovereignty." To what extent do you agree with this statement? In your answer, consider the perspectives of short-term and long-term.
items.answer: Sovereignty is pooled and constrained, but states remain the main actors.
items.markingKey: Paper 3 (b) indicative content - for: WTO and EU rules, IMF conditions; TNC and digital platform power. Against: states still control borders, taxation and laws (Brexit, tariffs); powerful states shape global rules. Judgement: Sovereignty is pooled and constrained, but states remain the main actors. Markbands [16]: 14-16 well-structured, balanced argument that synthesises HL concepts (power, places, processes, possibilities) across scales; perspectives evaluated explicitly; detailed, located evidence; substantiated conclusion. 11-13 balanced with developed evidence but synthesis uneven. 8-10 some evaluation, evidence partly developed. 5-7 mainly descriptive. 1-4 little relevant knowledge.

items.stem: Explain the arguments that geographers use to support the view that supply-chain disruptions are the greatest economic risk of globalisation.
items.answer: frequent and costly (COVID, chips, Red Sea); affect consumers worldwide
items.markingKey: Paper 3 (a) indicative content: frequent and costly (COVID, chips, Red Sea); affect consumers worldwide; financial crises cause deeper and longer recessions; debt crises harm the poorest countries most. Markbands [12]: 10-12 detailed, accurate explanation with well-developed, located examples and clear links between factors; 7-9 accurate explanation, examples partly developed; 4-6 some relevant knowledge, mostly descriptive; 1-3 little relevant knowledge.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "sovereignty".
items.answer: The authority of a state to govern itself without outside interference
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: the authority of a state to govern itself without outside interference. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "A sudden fall in asset values and failure of financial institutions, which spreads through credit markets to the wider economy"?
items.answer: financial crisis
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of financial crisis.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "China plus one"?
options: Malicious software that encrypts a victim's data until a ransom is paid
A strategy of keeping production in China while adding another location such as Vietnam or India
Returning production previously offshored back to the home country
A state whose government has lost control of its territory and cannot provide basic services or security
items.answer: A strategy of keeping production in China while adding another location such as Vietnam or India
items.markingKey: B. "China plus one" is a strategy of keeping production in China while adding another location such as Vietnam or India.

items.stem: Explain why cyberterrorism is a growing geopolitical risk.
items.answer: Economies and infrastructure (power, water, health, finance) depend on interconnected digital systems; attacks are cheap, can be launched remotely and anonymously, and can cascade across borders.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Economies and infrastructure (power, water, health, finance) depend on interconnected digital systems; attacks are cheap, can be launched remotely and anonymously, and can cascade across borders. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Briefly explain why high debt can be a risk for low- and middle-income countries.
items.answer: Debt service absorbs export earnings and government revenue; rising interest rates and currency falls increase repayments; default cuts access to credit and imports of food and fuel, as in Sri Lanka 2022.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Debt service absorbs export earnings and government revenue; rising interest rates and currency falls increase repayments; default cuts access to credit and imports of food and fuel, as in Sri Lanka 2022. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Distinguish between reshoring and nearshoring.
items.answer: Reshoring brings production back to the home country; nearshoring moves it to a nearby country with lower costs, such as Mexico for the USA or Poland and Türkiye for Western Europe.
items.markingKey: Reshoring brings production back to the home country; nearshoring moves it to a nearby country with lower costs, such as Mexico for the USA or Poland and Türkiye for Western Europe. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: "Cyberattacks only affect computers, not people." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Attacks on hospitals, power grids and fuel supplies can endanger lives and halt economies.
items.markingKey: Attacks on hospitals, power grids and fuel supplies can endanger lives and halt economies. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain the difference between just-in-case and just-in-time.
items.answer: Just-in-time keeps minimal stock for efficiency; just-in-case holds larger buffer stocks and diversified suppliers for resilience.
items.markingKey: Just-in-time keeps minimal stock for efficiency; just-in-case holds larger buffer stocks and diversified suppliers for resilience. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: "International cooperation is always effective." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Unequal power and national interests limit cooperation, e.g. vaccine nationalism during COVID-19.
items.markingKey: Unequal power and national interests limit cooperation, e.g. vaccine nationalism during COVID-19. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A fieldwork survey recorded the views of 60 residents interviewed about a new foreign-owned factory in Bac Ninh, Vietnam: support 9, neutral 8, oppose 43. Test the null hypothesis that there is no preference between categories using the chi-squared test (χ² = Σ(O − E)²/E; critical value at 0.05 for 2 degrees of freedom = 5.99).
items.answer: E = 20 per category; χ² = 39.70; df = 2; significant - reject the null hypothesis
items.markingKey: M1 expected 60/3 = 20; M1 Σ(O − E)²/E; A1 χ² = 39.70; A1 df = 2; R1 compare with 5.99: reject H₀.

items.stem: Between 1995 and 2005 the internet users in an East African country changed from 44.2 to 76.8 million. Calculate the percentage change over the period.
items.markingKey: M1 (new − old) ÷ old × 100 = (76.8 − 44.2) ÷ 44.2 × 100; A1 +73.8% (sign or "increase/decrease" required).

items.stem: Indonesia imposes a 25% tariff on imported rice. The world price is US$640 per tonne. Imports were 490 thousand tonnes a year and fall by 30% after the tariff. Calculate the import price including the tariff and the annual tariff revenue (US$ million). Explain one disadvantage of the tariff for consumers or firms in the importing country.
items.answer: price = 640 × 1.25 = US$800 per tonne; imports 343 thousand; revenue = 640 × 0.25 × 343,000 = US$54.9 million; disadvantage: higher prices for consumers and higher costs for firms using the good, and possible retaliation against exports.
items.markingKey: A1 price US$800; M1 new import quantity 343 thousand; A1 revenue US$54.9 million. R1 disadvantage.

items.stem: With reference to the war in Ukraine, explain how it illustrates conflict and global interdependence.
items.answer: From 2022 Black Sea grain exports were disrupted and European gas prices rose to record levels. War in one region transmitted price shocks worldwide.
items.markingKey: Context (From 2022 Black Sea grain exports were disrupted and European gas prices rose to record levels.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: War in one region transmitted price shocks worldwide. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to conflict and global interdependence.

items.stem: The USA imposes a 35% tariff on washing machines from Asia. The world price is US$400 per machine. Imports were 830 thousand machines a year and fall by 15% after the tariff. Calculate the import price including the tariff and the annual tariff revenue (US$ million). Explain one disadvantage of the tariff for consumers or firms in the importing country.
items.answer: price = 400 × 1.35 = US$540 per machine; imports 706 thousand; revenue = 400 × 0.35 × 705,500 = US$98.8 million; disadvantage: higher prices for consumers and higher costs for firms using the good, and possible retaliation against exports.
items.markingKey: A1 price US$540; M1 new import quantity 706 thousand; A1 revenue US$98.8 million. R1 disadvantage.

items.stem: Using TSMC's factories in Arizona as an example, explain reshoring strategic industries.
items.answer: Supported by the CHIPS Act, TSMC committed over US$65 billion (later raised further) to chip fabs near Phoenix. Governments subsidise domestic production of critical goods.
items.markingKey: Context (Supported by the CHIPS Act, TSMC committed over US$65 billion (later raised further) to chip fabs near Phoenix.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Governments subsidise domestic production of critical goods. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to reshoring strategic industries.

items.stem: India imposes a 35% tariff on smartphones. The world price is US$130 per phone. Imports were 740 thousand phones a year and fall by 15% after the tariff. Calculate the import price including the tariff and the annual tariff revenue (US$ million). Explain one disadvantage of the tariff for consumers or firms in the importing country.
items.answer: price = 130 × 1.35 = US$176 per phone; imports 629 thousand; revenue = 130 × 0.35 × 629,000 = US$28.6 million; disadvantage: higher prices for consumers and higher costs for firms using the good, and possible retaliation against exports.
items.markingKey: A1 price US$176; M1 new import quantity 629 thousand; A1 revenue US$28.6 million. R1 disadvantage.

items.stem: Briefly analyse two contrasting points of view on the statement: "Supply-chain disruptions are the greatest economic risk of globalisation."
items.answer: Supply chains are a major and growing risk, but financial crises remain the most damaging.
items.markingKey: For: frequent and costly (COVID, chips, Red Sea). Against: financial crises cause deeper and longer recessions. [4]: 1 mark for a valid argument for, 1 for its development; 1 mark for a valid argument against, 1 for its development; generic points without geographical context are capped at 2.

items.stem:
Study the infographic / visual stimulus described below.

Table: share of US goods imports (%) - China: 2017 21.6, 2023 13.9; Mexico: 2017 13.4, 2023 15.4; Vietnam: 2017 2.0, 2023 3.6.

(a) Calculate the percentage change in China's share between 2017 and 2023. [4]
(b) Using the resource and your own knowledge, suggest reasons for the changes shown. [6]
items.answer: (a) (13.9 − 21.6)/21.6 × 100 = -35.6% (b) US tariffs on Chinese goods from 2018, firms diversifying supply chains after COVID-19 (China plus one), and nearshoring to Mexico under USMCA.

items.stem: To what extent do you agree that cyberterrorism is now a greater risk to global interactions than physical terrorism?
items.answer: Cyber risks are growing fastest, but physical conflict remains the more severe disruption.

items.stem: "Economic interdependence increases risk more than it increases prosperity." To what extent do you agree with this statement? In your answer, consider the perspectives of different stakeholders.
items.answer: Interdependence increases exposure to shocks, but its benefits generally outweigh the risks if resilience is built in.
items.markingKey: Paper 3 (b) indicative content - for: contagion (2008), supply shocks (COVID, Ever Given); debt crises. Against: trade and investment lifted billions from poverty; interdependence allows recovery support and diversification.
